newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar climbs strongly as G7 removes worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar climbs strongly as G7 removes worries.

text.p: The dollar climbed strongly in early European trade on Monday after finance ministers of the G7 industrialised countries made comments which removed market worries about the strength of the U.S. currency.

On equity markets, the stronger dollar and prospects of cheaper exports boosted some Frankfurt stocks and Paris was encouraged by two opinion polls supporting the ruling coalition in the upcoming election.

The dollar surged to 37-month highs against the mark after the ministers said on Sunday that major currency misaligments had been corrected and that excessive currency volatility and deviations from fundamentals were undesirable.
Analysts said the remarks lacked aggressiveness and had made dollar bulls comfortable.
The U.S. currency strengthened by nearly a pfennig and over half a yen in early transactions compared to the levels seen in late Friday's European trade.

The market view in the light of the G7 statement appeared to be that the authorities would tolerate a strong dollar as long as it did not move rapidly, analysts said, citing a remark made by Bank of England Governor Eddie George after the meeting.
George said G7 officials felt the foreign exchange environment was "in pretty good shape" and that no need had been expressed at the meeting for an action plan to deal with future currency moves.
Relief over the lack of dollar-dampening G7 comments drove the dollar against the yen to within a shade of a 55-month high reached earlier this month.

"Providing we don't see the dollar surging above 1.75 (marks) and 130 (yen), the perception is that the authorities are not going to intervene in a coordinated or aggressive fashion," said one expert.
But euphoria was clouded because the G7 had sounded a warning note on trade imbalances.

The meeting emphasised the importance of avoiding currency moves that could lead to a re-emergence of large trade imbalances. They named no names, but markets saw this as a reference to Japan's swelling, politically sensitive trade surplus with the U.S..
In equity markets, French stocks made the strongest running moving ahead 0.6 percent after two polls gave the ruling centre-right coalition a sizeable majority in the upcoming parliamentary election.
The bourse was also underpinned by the dollar's strength, but its advance was muted by caution ahead of a string of U.S. economic indicators due out this week, brokers said.
A poll published in Monday's Le Figaro saw the centre-right winning the May 25-June 1 election with 329 seats, with the Socialists, other left and ecologists obtaining 202.

An different poll published on Sunday also showed the RPR-UDF coalition and conservative allies winning. The two polls were expected to provide some reassurance for the French financial markets, which were jolted last week by a poll predicting a tight race.
London shares barely moved in early trade, with the market weighed down by New York's 0.79 percent losses on Friday and political uncertainty over the outcome of Thursday's UK election.
Talk of an interest rate rise next week of as much as a half point next week also depressed investors.
Dealers also said markets were likely fret over U.S. figures this week -- culminating in the key employment report on Friday -- which could renew fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates.
"There will be some nervous expectations of what the week has in store," said one.
In Frankfurt, the picture was mixed with trade slipping a few points but deals on the computerised IBIS index climbing nearly 0.5 percent, boosted by gains in the dollar.
STOCKS AT 0915 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 3.5 points at 4,373.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 15.09 points at 2,551.35.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 2.00 at 3,372.10.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7327 against the mark versus 1.7235 in late European trade on Friday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.73 from 125.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $341.75 an ounce in early trade after ending at $342.45 in London on Friday. Silver unchanged at was at $4.73.
